I checked each claim in the draft against the policy.

- "Good tea, no fuss." This is plain and warm, and it makes no superlative. It's fine.
- "Certified organic by the Soil Association" matches the allowlist wording exactly. The certificate was renewed in 2026, so it is current.
- "packed by hand in Bristol" is a shortened form of "Every tin is packed by hand in Bristol". The meaning is the same and it is backed by Operations, so it's fine.
- "free UK delivery on orders over £25" matches the shipping policy wording exactly.

I found no banned words, no health or environmental claims, no invented numbers, no urgency and no guarantees. The spelling is UK. It is a hero line on our own landing page, so no disclosure label applies. Sam is the approver for everything public, so it still needs Sam's sign-off before it goes live. That is a process step and not a change to the copy.
